stem: Which statement about human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination is accurate?

options.A: It treats established HPV infection and removes existing HPV-related lesions after an abnormal screening result.
options.B: It prevents new infections with vaccine HPV types and works best when given before exposure to HPV.
options.C: It should be delayed until after sexual activity begins so prior HPV exposure can improve the vaccine response.
options.D: It removes the need for recommended cervical cancer screening because vaccination prevents every oncogenic HPV type.

rationale: CDC guidance states that HPV vaccination prevents new HPV infections but does not treat existing HPV infection or disease, and it works best when given before exposure to HPV. CDC also states that HPV vaccination does not replace recommended cervical cancer screening. Therefore B is correct. A incorrectly describes treatment rather than prevention, C delays vaccination until exposure is more likely, and D falsely states that vaccination eliminates screening and covers every oncogenic HPV type.
educational_objective: Teach that HPV vaccination is preventive, works best before HPV exposure, does not treat established infection or disease, and does not eliminate recommended cervical cancer screening.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_document_title: HPV Vaccine Recommendations; Vaccines (Shots) and Cancer; Reducing Risk for Cervical Cancer
source_version_date: Current CDC HPV guidance; cancer vaccination page January 16, 2025; currentness live-rechecked August 16, 2026
source_locator: HPV Vaccine Recommendations > Keep in mind: prevents new HPV infections, does not treat existing infections/diseases, works best before exposure. Vaccines (Shots) and Cancer / Reducing Risk for Cervical Cancer: HPV vaccine does not substitute for recommended cervical screening and vaccinated people should continue appropriate screening.
source_claim_supported: HPV vaccination prevents new vaccine-type HPV infections, is most effective before exposure, does not treat established infection/disease, and does not eliminate recommended cervical screening.

source_original.stem: Which statement about human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination is accurate?

options.A: It treats established HPV infection and removes existing lesions after an abnormal screening result.
options.B: It prevents new infections with vaccine HPV types and works best when given before exposure.
options.C: It should be started only after sexual activity begins so prior exposure can stimulate vaccine response.
options.D: It removes the need for recommended cervical screening because vaccination prevents every oncogenic HPV type.

source_original.rationale: HPV vaccination prevents new HPV infections and is most effective before exposure. It does not treat established infection or existing lesions and does not eliminate recommended screening. Option B is correct. C incorrectly delays vaccination until after exposure is more likely.
source_original.source_detail: HPV vaccination guidance: vaccination prevents new HPV infections and works best before exposure; it does not treat existing HPV infection or disease. Routine vaccination is recommended at ages 11-12 (can start at 9), with catch-up through age 26 if not adequately vaccinated. Current CDC HPV vaccine recommendations live-rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Health Promotion and Maintenance: preventive screening, immunization, pregnancy/reproductive health and age/risk-appropriate teaching activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Retained the prevention construct and key B. Tightened all options to current CDC wording and added direct screening corroboration so the item distinguishes prevention of new infection from treatment and from cervical screening obligations without relying on age-schedule details that are unnecessary to the construct.

audit_findings.source_authority: Current CDC HPV and cancer-prevention guidance; official NCSBN 2026 blueprint
audit_findings.exact_locator: CDC HPV Vaccine Recommendations > Keep in mind; CDC cancer vaccination/cervical cancer prevention pages on screening after vaccination
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item uses only stable current prevention/treatment/screening principles and avoids unnecessary dosing-schedule details.

distractor_audit.A: Incorrect because HPV vaccination does not treat existing infection or disease.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect because vaccination works best before exposure rather than being delayed until sexual activity begins.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect because vaccination does not cover every oncogenic type and does not replace recommended cervical screening.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only B correctly describes the vaccine's preventive function and timing principle without adding a false treatment or screening claim.
audit_findings.cueing: All alternatives are patient-teaching statements about vaccine purpose/timing/screening.
audit_findings.blueprint: Health Promotion and Maintenance — immunization and preventive screening education.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Rechecked current CDC HPV recommendations, screening guidance, all options, rationale, objective, NCSBN mapping, ambiguity and cueing. B remained uniquely correct.
